feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Spain's September 2026 was its warmest since national records began in 1961
entry.summary: Spain's national weather agency put September's mean at 22.5 °C, 3.4 °C above normal and the first September warmer than an average summer. — Sources: AEMET, September 2026 climate summary, 16 October 2026

entry.title: El Niño strengthened again, with weekly Niño-3.4 at 2.4 °C above normal
entry.summary: The US Climate Prediction Center's 13 October update puts weekly Niño-3.4 at 2.4 °C above normal and keeps an 83% chance October to December reaches historic strength. — Sources: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO weekly update, 13 October 2026 · Bureau of Meteorology, Climate Driver Update, 13 October 2026

entry.title: Mumbai, India reached 38.2 °C, its second-hottest October day on record
entry.summary: Santacruz in Mumbai recorded 38.2 °C on 12 October, 5.1 °C above normal and second only to an October day in 2015. — Sources: Time Out Mumbai, citing India Meteorological Department, 13 October 2026 · The Bridge Chronicle, 9 October 2026

entry.title: Australia's Northern Territory, northern Western Australia and Tasmania face a severe heatwave
entry.summary: Australia's Bureau of Meteorology assessed a severe heatwave for the Northern Territory's Top End and Tiwi Islands, Western Australia's Kimberley, Pilbara and North Interior, and south-eastern Tasmania from 17 to 19 October, continuing in the Top End to around 23 October. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, heatwave assessment, 17 October 2026

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany has stalled at about 10 centimetres
entry.summary: Germany's federal gauge at Kaub read 10 centimetres on the morning of 17 October. — Sources: Pegelonline, Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration, Kaub gauge, 1 to 17 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: Kaub first fell below zero on 25 September, and minus 6 centimetres on 1 October is the record low
entry.summary: This page reported on 10 October that the Rhine at Kaub first fell below zero on 1 October. Germany's federal gauge data show it first read minus 1 centimetre on 25 September. — Sources: Pegelonline, Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration, Kaub gauge, 20 September to 1 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: Hungary's Paks nuclear plant ran at reduced output in August and was never fully shut
entry.summary: This page reported on 15 October that Paks shut down completely on 2 August. — Sources: NucNet, 3 August 2026 · Euronews, 10 August 2026 · CGTN, 24 August 2026 · Montel, 3 August 2026

entry.title: Singapore's haze reached the very unhealthy band for the first time this year
entry.summary: Singapore's 24-hour PSI peaked at 229 in the central region on 16 October, after the west reached 205 on 14 October and 212 on 15 October. — Sources: National Environment Agency, hourly PSI data via data.gov.sg, 9 to 17 October 2026 · National Environment Agency, haze situation updates, 13 to 16 October 2026 · AsiaOne, 16 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: Singapore's air did not return to moderate on 11 or 14 October
entry.summary: This page reported a moderate PSI of 56 to 81 for 11 October and a moderate reading on the morning of 14 October. The 11 October figures came from a 2023 report. — Sources: National Environment Agency, hourly PSI data via data.gov.sg, 11 and 14 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's daily fire-hotspot count is swinging between about 11,000 and 20,000
entry.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Forestry counted 20,334 hotspots on 14 October, 19,712 on 15 October, 11,658 on 16 October and 11,041 on 17 October, against a peak of 24,952 on 8 October. — Sources: Ministry of Forestry SiPongi data via databoks.katadata.co.id, 14 to 17 October 2026 · The Star, 12 October 2026

entry.title: Johor, Malaysia closed all 1,198 of its schools twice in a week as haze returned
entry.summary: Johor closed its schools on 8 and 9 October and again from 12 to 16 October, affecting 617,258 students across 1,198 schools. — Sources: The Star, 10 October 2026 · New Straits Times, 10 October 2026 · Malay Mail and Business Today, 17 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire-season respiratory infections passed 280,000 cases
entry.summary: Indonesia recorded 283,270 acute respiratory infection cases by 13 October, up from 113,336 on 9 September. — Sources: Mongabay, 16 October 2026 · The Edge, 17 October 2026

entry.title: Malaysia ordered employers to give N95 masks to outdoor workers during the haze
entry.summary: Malaysia's Health Ministry directive of 16 October requires employers to provide N95 masks to outdoor workers. — Sources: The Star, 16 October 2026

entry.title: A UK bill on maximum workplace temperature has its second reading set for 13 November
entry.summary: The Maximum Workplace Temperature Bill, introduced on 13 July, would set up an independent body to recommend a maximum safe workplace temperature. — Sources: UK Parliament, Maximum Workplace Temperature Bill, bills.parliament.uk, updated 12 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: Luxembourg's heat-inspection figures run to early July
entry.summary: This page reported on 16 October that Luxembourg ruled out a binding workplace heat limit, with 46 heat inspections so far in 2026. — Sources: Paperjam, 7 July 2026
